subject: Physics
basis: Every ruling names the section that teaches it and was checked against the
book TEXT via generated-papers/physics-corpus.json, not against section
titles. A title match is not evidence: JEE's Transformers has no heading in
the State Board AC chapter, yet the topic is taught in full one chapter
earlier, and a title-only pass would have called it a gap.
Coverage is judged on what the exam DEMANDS, not on how our bank happens to
solve it. Absent rulings are absent on purpose - an unreviewed subtopic has
no row at all, so 'not yet assessed' stays distinguishable from 'covered'.

stateBoard.note: 13.5 derives the voltage-current relation for R, L and C individually; reactance appears 66 times in the chapter.

ncert.note: NOT in NCERT at all: 'LC oscillation' occurs ZERO times across all four Physics volumes, both years - the rationalised edition dropped it. The State Board still teaches it at 13.7, so this is a gap on the NCERT side, the reverse of the usual direction.
